The Story of Sumitra the Merchant

I bow to Lord Jina, the bestower of all happiness, and I write the story of Sumitra the merchant, who loved dharma.

During the reign of King Suvarnavarma and Queen Suvarnashri of Ayodhya, there lived a famous merchant named Sumitra. The merchant had extreme love for Jain dharma. One night, Sumitra was practising kayotsarga meditation in his own house. Seeing his steadfastness in meditation and the firmness of his mental states, a god became suspicious and decided to test him, wondering if this was mere pretence.

In the test, the god took control of all the merchant's property, wife, children, and everything. The merchant's cry for help reached him. His wife and children, weeping, fell at his feet and made heart-rending pleas: 'Save us, save us!' Everything that should not have happened, happened. But the merchant did not break his incomplete meditation — he remained unmoved as before.

Seeing this superhuman steadiness, the god was greatly pleased. He praised the merchant with a hundred mouths. Finally, revealing his true form, he gifted the merchant a celestial knowledge called Sankochi — a knowledge that moves through the sky — and returned to heaven. Seeing the merchant's spiritual power, many people embraced Jain dharma — some took monastic vows, some lay vows, and some only right faith.

The lotus feet of Lord Jina bestow supreme happiness and carry beings across the ocean of existence. Therefore, worthy souls should worship, praise, meditate upon, and remember the Lord for the attainment of happiness.

This story teaches that true spiritual practice is tested not in comfortable circumstances but in times of extreme crisis. Sumitra's meditation was not broken even when his entire world — family, wealth, everything — was threatened. His unwavering steadiness in the face of total loss demonstrated the depth of his spiritual attainment. The wise should understand that genuine spiritual progress is revealed not by how one meditates in peace but by how one remains centred in the midst of chaos.
